PROSPER_primary_prevention_subgroup.notes: The trial report (Lancet 2002, PMID 12457784) has no PMC/CC BY copy (Europe PMC license=None, isOpenAccess=N), so its full text was NOT read. The PubMed abstract does not report the primary-prevention subgroup HR or say which subgroups were predefined. FDA: the current Pravachol label does not mention PROSPER, and no PROSPER review turned up in the NDA 019898 listing. HR 0.94 (0.77-1.15) appears only in two third-party CC BY reviews that cite the Lancet paper; they are secondary sources, not the trial report. The only 'pre-defined' statement is in the PROSPER group's 2013 extended-follow-up paper and covers that paper's own subgroup analyses, so it does NOT show that the 2002 primary-prevention subgroup was prespecified. Primary-source spans for both requested items: SOURCE_ABSENT. State PARTIAL = secondary-source HR only. Wording difference: PMC11588824 paraphrases the endpoint as 'coronary heart disease death, or non-fatal myocardial infarction or stroke'.

EMPHASIS-HF_hyperkalaemia_K_gt_5.5.notes: The claimed lab counts 158/1336 (eplerenone) v 96/1340 (placebo) were NOT found in any open source. The abstract gives percentages only (11.8% v 7.2%). CT.gov posts no lab-potassium outcome; it has investigator-reported MedDRA hyperkalaemia AEs (a different measure with different denominators) and an adjudicated hyperkalaemia-hospitalisation outcome. FDA Inspra labels and reviews contain EPHESUS data only, with no EMPHASIS-HF supplement. EMA EPAR was NOT checked (Inspra is believed to be nationally rather than centrally authorised in the EU; this was not verified in this session). The NEJM full text is not open, so it was not read. Counts and denominators: SOURCE_ABSENT. Arithmetic note (not a sourced value): 158/1336 = 11.8% and 96/1340 = 7.2%, so the claim matches the abstract percentages, but the abstract alone cannot confirm the counts or denominators.

The 8% vs 7% span cites jupiter_11.pdf.txt, the pypdf text of jupiter_11.pdf. Suggestion: the captain could OCR jupiter_9.pdf (FDA, public domain) to look for an age-subgroup muscle table.

COPPS_POAF_substudy.notes: Table 3 of the Circulation 2011 paper could not be checked: it has no PMC/CC BY copy (license=None), so the full text was NOT read. CT.gov has no posted results and EU CTR has no public results. The abstract gives only the total (336) and 12.0% v 22.0%, with no per-arm counts or denominators. The only open per-arm counts are in a THIRD-PARTY meta-analysis table (PMC9937735, CC BY): colchicine 20/169, placebo 37/167. These equal the harness's inferred values, so the table may be the same kind of inference and is not independent confirmation. No open source states 35 placebo events. Arithmetic flag (not a sourced value): 20/169 = 11.8% and 37/167 = 22.2%, which do not round to the abstract's 12.0% and 22.0%, so the 169/167 split is unverified too. Primary-source per-arm counts and denominators: SOURCE_ABSENT.
